events.message: Email 1, draft 1: "Beyond Supabase’s built-in sender"
events.subject: Beyond Supabase’s built-in sender
events.preview_text: See the hook, Edge Function, template, and domain requirements.
events.body:
Supabase’s built-in sender is a test-only, rate-limited path. Moving auth email off it still leaves a replacement route to implement.

Loops is an email sending platform for SaaS that can handle Supabase Auth email through the Send Email Hook. Supabase calls an Edge Function you deploy; that function verifies the request and sends the matching Loops transactional email.

Each configured auth action type needs its own Loops template. A verified Loops sending domain is also required before those messages can send.

The Supabase documentation lays out this architecture and its required components, so you can judge whether the hook, Edge Function, action-specific templates, and verified domain fit your Auth setup before implementing it.

Selected audience (explicit constraints): A Supabase or Clerk app team moving auth and onboarding email off the platform's built-in defaults before launch.
The context and problem reports below describe observed members of this market, not established experiences or installed tools of this recipient. The campaign request controls which job this email addresses; do not require a link to an unrequested integration in your doubts or click requirements.
Observed context (grounded; applicability must be checked): Small software teams running Supabase Auth in a real app reach a point — beta registration, App Store submission, opening public signup — where the platform's built-in email sender stops being adequate and auth mail (signup confirmation, recovery, invites, magic links) must be moved onto their own SMTP provider or Send Email hook on a verified domain. events.subject: Map your Supabase Auth emails
events.preview_text: Inspect the Edge Function, templates, and sending-domain requirements.
events.body:
Loops, an email sending platform for SaaS, can send Supabase Auth email using Supabase’s Send Email Hook.

The hook calls a Supabase Edge Function, which verifies the request and sends the matching Loops transactional template. Each configured auth action type uses its own template, keeping the email tied to the action that triggered it.

This route requires you to deploy the Edge Function, create those action-specific templates, and verify a Loops sending domain before messages can send.

Loops’ Supabase integration documentation shows this specific Auth Hook architecture and its required components. Use it to decide whether the Edge Function, template structure, and verified sending domain fit your Auth email setup.
events.call_to_action: Review the Loops Auth Hook docs
